key_insight: A passive nematic can develop periodic and irregular dynamics under a temporally steady, spatially varying flow, without velocity fluctuations or hydrodynamic feedback.
engineering_relevance: Steady forcing alone may not ensure stable nematic alignment, a consideration when designing flow-controlled liquid-crystal systems.
method: Model planar nematic order under prescribed steady Kolmogorov flow.
Use bifurcation and phase-space analyses to characterise transitions as flow strength increases.
Develop two- and five-mode reduced-order models to identify dynamical mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stationary-to-periodic-to-irregular transitions, a saddle-node infinite-period onset captured by a two-mode model, and the broader progression reproduced by a five-mode truncation.
watch_item: The model excludes velocity fluctuations and hydrodynamic feedback, so its predictions require validation in fully coupled flows.
paper_title: Complex nematic dynamics driven by steady Kolmogorov flows
